panels.rationale: Single lateral radiograph of the right foot (marked 'R') from an article titled 'Gas gangrene and osteomyelitis of the foot in a diabetic patient treated with tea tree oil.' The caption explicitly states the X-ray reveals soft-tissue gas consistent with gangrene, and the image shows dark lucencies (arrows) tracking through the soft tissues of the foot, matching the vocabulary finding of gas dissecting along fascial planes. Soft-tissue gas on plain radiograph is a classic manifestation of clostridial myonecrosis (gas gangrene). No age or ethnicity is stated in the caption or in-text; skin tone is not assessable on radiograph.

in_text_mentions: X-ray images should be obtained in patients with diabetic foot ulcers to evaluate for the presence of osteomyelitis and gas in the soft tissues. Osteomyelitis was noted in this case; however, the soft tissue gas is much more prominent (Figure 3). The presence of gas on x-ray of the affected area should prompt the clinician to obtain images up to the next proximal joint in order to ascertain the extent of the infection [10]. In cases where gas is not seen, but deep space soft tissue infection is suspected, computed tomography (CT) or magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) may be appropriate.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (a, b, c). a: Human patient H&E section showing coagulative necrosis of skeletal muscle (ghost myofibers with loss of stainable nuclei), a hallmark of clostridial myonecrosis/gas gangrene in this Clostridium septicum case. Disease attribution is direct from the caption and article title. b: Human patient H&E section showing edematous adipocytes and fibrous tissue with rare stainable nuclei, explicitly captioned as soft tissue necrosis in the same Clostridium septicum gas gangrene case. The manifestation is disease-specific but has no exact vocabulary key (the only necrosis key is muscle-specific), so it is recorded in proposed_findings rather than misattributed to muscle. c: Gram-stained human tissue section showing numerous large blunt-ended (boxcar) Gram-positive rods between necrotic cells, the classic microbiologic signature of Clostridium in clostridial myonecrosis. Directly supported by caption and in-text mention.

Numerous large Gram-positive blunt-ended rods were apparent throughout the necrotic soft tissue in sections stained with Gram stain. (Figure 2(c)).

panels.figure_caption: Preoperative CT scan. (a) shows an axial slice of the pelvis a little proximally from the acetabula with a massive infestation of the gluteal muscles and the intrusion of the infection into the retroperitoneal space in the true pelvis though the sciatic notch (arrow). (b) shows a sagittal reconstruction slice with extensive infestation of the whole circumference of the thigh. Gluteal musculature, the extensor muscles (quadriceps and rectus), and hamstrings are affected. (c) shows a coronary reconstruction with again massive affection of the thigh. It also indicates the disseminated infestation of the retroperitoneum with evidence of gas (arrows). (d) shows gas next to the vascular pedicle of the right kidney (arrow). (e) shows the thickened ascending colon (left arrow) and again retroperitoneal gas (right arrow).

It showed the affection of almost the entire right lower extremity and, worse, the intrusion into the retroperitoneal space ranging up to the vascular pedicle of the right kidney. Furthermore, the CT scan revealed a long-distance thickening of the ascending colon allowing a chronic inflammation or a neoplasm as a differential diagnosis. panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (a, b). a: Sagittal CT on initial admission shows anterolateral soft tissue swelling at T11/12 with gas lucencies in the epidural space. In a case explicitly attributed to gas gangrene (clostridial myonecrosis), gas within soft tissue/epidural space is a direct manifestation of the gas-forming clostridial infection, so the panel is diagnostic of the target disease. b: Axial CT at T11/12 shows a gas-containing epidural abscess (dark gas bubbles in the canal). Gas production is the hallmark of clostridial infection and the article title attributes the epidural abscess/osteomyelitis to gas gangrene, so this is a specific diagnostic manifestation of clostridial myonecrosis rather than an unrelated complication.

A: Pelvis X-ray of a human patient explicitly captioned as clostridial gas gangrene caused by Clostridium septicum, with a red circle highlighting gas in the gluteus muscle; intramuscular/soft-tissue gas on plain film is a textbook radiologic manifestation of clostridial myonecrosis. B: Axial CT of the same captioned clostridial gas gangrene patient, red circle marking the extent of gas formation in the gluteal soft tissues; extensive intramuscular gas on CT is a classic finding of clostridial myonecrosis. in_text_mentions: Ultrasound, conventional X‐ray, CT, or MRI can be used for radiological imaging. Ultrasound is immediately applicable but highly dependent on the skills of the examiner. X‐ray might already show gas in the affected tissue in cases of gas‐forming anaerobic bacteria (Fig. 5). CT scans show involvement of the fascia (lack of enhancement after administration of contrast medium), fascial plane thickening, and intramuscular fluid collection 38 . In addition, they provide information about the proliferation of the infection (Fig. 5).

source_variant.context: Sagittal noncontrast CT of the abdomen and pelvis shows a gravid uterus with a fetus and extensive gas bubbles in the fetal skull, thorax, abdomen, and soft tissues, along with air in the umbilical and placental vessels, an acute fetal calvarial fracture, and air in the maternal vaginal canal.
source_variant.context_summary: Sagittal noncontrast CT of the abdomen and pelvis shows a gravid uterus with a fetus and extensive gas bubbles in the fetal skull, thorax, abdomen, and soft tissues, along with air in the umbilical and placental vessels, an acute fetal calvarial fracture, and air in the maternal vaginal canal.
source_variant.figure_caption: CT of the abdomen and pelvis without contrast sagittal view. Gravid uterus with the fetus measuring up to 36 cm from the calvarium to the lower pelvis. There is air in the abdominal cavity, the umbilical cord, and placental vessels (left arrow). There are extensive gas bubbles in the subdural space of the skull, thoracic cavity, abdominal cavity, and anterior soft tissue of the head and neck (middle arrow). There is an acute fracture of the fetal calvarium and there are adjacent large locules of air in the maternal vaginal canal (right arrow). The fetal bowel is dilated.
